intro: Stonkr Bot sells a browser-based AI trading desk with a US$250 entry. Before the first deposit, it is worth asking which of the published claims survive contact with the platform own fine print.
The platform is browser-only, with no app to install. Signals arrive from the models, trades execute through a broker partner, and the US$250 minimum opens access to 10 assets and the demo.
Our method is a desk review: no funded account, no trades. We read the published material in full, including unfilled placeholders and contradictions, and scored five fixed dimensions.
whatItClaims: Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
whatWeChecked: The demo claim: practice account confirmed in the signup flow.
The payout promise: within-a-day wording without processing detail.
The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Fill in the registration form and activate the account via the confirmation email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Transfer the US$250 minimum - the sum stays in your trading balance, it is not a fee.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Choose the risk settings and execution mode, then start with the practice balance.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: One figure doing two different jobs.
Return claims without verification.
Payout wording without processing detail.
No named regulator or licence.
redFlags: A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.
Performance language with no dates attached.
A broker relationship described in one vague sentence.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

bottomLine: Stonkr Bot reads as a functioning AI trading service with the standard package, and the product itself clears the bar for a cautious trial.
We rate it 4.8 with conditions: the platform is usable, the published claims are not all verifiable, and the US$250 minimum is the right size for testing either.
